description: The chickpea leaf is healthy with no visible signs of disease or stress.
treatement: Maintain regular monitoring and good agricultural practices.

description: Alternaria leaf spot causes brown, circular lesions with concentric rings on chickpea leaves. The disease thrives in warm, humid conditions.
treatement: Apply fungicides containing mancozeb or chlorothalonil. Remove infected leaves and improve air circulation.

description: Leaves are drying out, which can be caused by water stress, nutrient deficiency, or late-stage disease.
treatement: Ensure adequate irrigation, check soil moisture, apply balanced fertilizers, and investigate underlying causes.

description: The hibiscus leaf is healthy with vibrant color and no visible signs of disease.
treatement: Continue regular care with proper watering and nutrient management.

description: Powdery mildew appears as a white, powdery coating on hibiscus leaves and stems. It thrives in warm, dry conditions.
treatement: Apply sulfur-based fungicides or neem oil. Improve air circulation and reduce humidity around the plant.

description: The leaf shows signs of insect feeding damage, with irregular holes or discoloration caused by pests.
treatement: Inspect for common hibiscus pests like spider mites or scale insects. Use appropriate insecticides or horticultural oils.

description: Leaves are drying and withering, possibly due to insufficient watering, low humidity, or temperature stress.
treatement: Increase watering frequency, mist the plant, maintain warm temperatures, and check for root problems.

description: Yellowing of leaves due to chlorophyll loss, typically caused by nutrient deficiency (iron, magnesium, or nitrogen).
treatement: Apply balanced fertilizer or specific micronutrient supplements. Improve soil drainage and pH if needed.

description: The mango leaf is healthy with normal coloration and no signs of disease or pest damage.
treatement: Maintain regular care schedule with appropriate watering and fertilization.

description: Powdery mildew on mango appears as white coating on leaves and flowers, reducing fruit quality.
treatement: Apply sulfur fungicides or wettable sulfur. Ensure good air circulation and avoid overhead watering.

description: Mango rust causes reddish-brown pustules on the underside of leaves, leading to premature leaf drop.
treatement: Apply copper-based fungicides. Remove and destroy infected leaves. Improve tree ventilation.

description: Bacterial leaf spot appears as small, dark, water-soaked lesions that may have a yellow halo on mango leaves.
treatement: Prune infected branches, apply copper fungicides, and improve drainage to reduce leaf wetness.

description: Mango leaves are drying due to water stress, root issues, or late-stage disease infection.
treatement: Check irrigation schedule, inspect roots for rot, and apply appropriate fungicides if disease is present.

description: Yellowing or pale leaves indicating deficiency of essential nutrients like nitrogen, iron, or magnesium.
treatement: Apply balanced fertilizer or specific micronutrient formulations. Conduct soil analysis to identify deficient nutrients.

description: The sorghum (Jowar) leaf is healthy with no visible signs of disease, pest damage, or nutrient deficiency.
treatement: Continue with regular maintenance and monitoring practices.

description: Anthracnose causes dark, elongated lesions with red borders on jowar leaves, leading to premature leaf death.
treatement: Use disease-resistant varieties, apply fungicides with active ingredient azoxystrobin, and practice crop rotation.

description: Jowar rust appears as reddish-brown pustules on leaf surfaces, reducing photosynthetic capacity.
treatement: Apply sulfur or rust-specific fungicides early. Remove infected plant material and improve field sanitation.

description: Black mold (sooty mold) appears as black coating on jowar leaves and grains, often following insect infestations.
treatement: Control insect vectors with appropriate insecticides. Remove heavily infected plant parts.

description: Jowar leaves are drying prematurely due to water stress, disease, or environmental conditions.
treatement: Ensure adequate irrigation, apply appropriate fungicides if disease is present, and check for pest damage.
